title: Add tool-calling agent loop w/ guardrails (max iterations, tool error handling, output limits)
author: Sabrina James
description:
## Summary
Implements the v1 “agent loop” for the Python RAG+Agents quickstart with tool calling and production-minded guardrails. The agent can:
- call registered tools via model tool-calls
- handle tool errors and surface actionable messages
- cap the number of iterations/tool calls to avoid runaway loops
- cap tool output size to avoid blowing up context windows / egress logs

This is intentionally opinionated and minimal: one agent loop implementation + a small tool abstraction so templates can add tools without pulling in a framework.

## Motivation
We keep seeing users build an initial “agent” that works in happy-path demos and then fails in production in predictable ways:
- infinite / long-running loops (cost spikes)
- tool output too large (latency spikes, context overflow)
- tool failures surfaced as vague 500s with no structured logs

This PR adds sane defaults + explicit guardrails and makes the failure modes obvious.

## What’s included
- `AgentRunner`: a deterministic loop that alternates between (a) calling the model and (b) executing tool calls until the model returns a final answer or we hit the guardrails.
- Tool registry + interface:
  - `Tool` protocol (name/description + `run(args)`) with simple JSON-serializable args
  - `ToolRegistry` for lookup + optional allowlist
- Guardrails:
  - `RW_AGENT_MAX_ITERATIONS` (default: 8)
  - `RW_TOOL_OUTPUT_MAX_BYTES` (default: 16384)
  - hard stop returns a user-facing error message and emits `agent.terminated_reason` in logs
- Tool error handling:
  - distinguishes `tool_not_found`, `tool_invalid_args`, `tool_execution_error`, `tool_output_too_large`
  - tool exceptions are caught, logged with a stable error code, and fed back to the model as a tool result message so it can recover (or choose to answer without the tool)
- Observability hooks (lightweight, no new dependencies):
  - structured logs include `agent.iteration`, `tool.name`, `tool.duration_ms`, `tool.error_code`, and `redwood_request_id` when available
  - spans are emitted where an OTel tracer is configured (no-ops otherwise)

## Implementation notes
- The loop follows the OpenAI-compatible tool calling shape used by Redwood’s hosted API.
- Tool results are truncated by bytes (utf-8) not characters to match how payload size actually behaves in transit.
- If the model repeatedly requests tools after max iterations, we stop and return a “guardrail exceeded” response with a clear remediation hint (increase limit, improve prompts/tool schema, or add a planner step).

## Tests
- Unit tests:
  - “happy path” tool call returns final answer
  - tool throws -> agent returns coherent response and logs error code
  - tool output truncation enforces max bytes
  - max iterations stop
- Smoke test updated to include a dummy tool call using the fake model adapter.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- Tool schema validation (JSON Schema) + better TS parity (tracked separately)
- Better “planner” prompt conventions + evals for tool reliability

---
### Checklist
- [x] guardrails documented in template README
- [x] errors have stable codes for troubleshooting
- [x] logs avoid printing tool args/outputs by default (to reduce accidental PII leakage)
- [x] CI green

Refs: ENG-4182
commits: feat(agent): add AgentRunner loop with tool calling and termination reasons
feat(tools): introduce Tool protocol + registry + default error types
feat(guardrails): cap iterations and tool output bytes; add env config
test(agent): add unit tests for tool failure + output truncation + max iterations
docs(template): document tool calling + guardrails + troubleshooting notes
review_conversation: Monica Patel: Can we make sure we don’t log tool args/outputs by default? I’m worried folks will add a “search CRM” tool and accidentally dump PII into logs.

Sabrina James (author): Yep — I updated the tool execution log line to record only tool name + duration + error_code. Args/outputs are explicitly omitted unless `RW_DEBUG_TOOL_PAYLOADS=1` is set (and even then we truncate). Also added a README callout in the Security section.
Christine Wong: Max iterations default of 12 feels high for a quickstart. Can we tighten to reduce runaway cost for PLG users?
Sabrina James (author): Agreed. Dropped default to 8 and added clearer messaging when we hit the limit (suggest improving prompt or tool). Kept env var override documented.
Dana Lo: For parity, can we keep error codes stable and short (snake_case) so the TS template can match?
Sabrina James (author): Done — standardized on: tool_not_found, tool_invalid_args, tool_execution_error, tool_output_too_large, max_iterations_exceeded.
Kaitlyn Nguyen: Any chance truncation could break UTF-8 and produce invalid JSON? Please confirm behavior.

Sabrina James (author): Truncation is byte-based but we truncate on utf-8 boundaries (encode/decode with errors='ignore') and wrap the result as plain text in the tool message. Added a test for multi-byte characters.
Monica Patel: Looks good after the logging change. Approving.
release_notes: Quickstart Python RAG+Agents template now includes a built-in tool-calling agent loop with safety guardrails (max iterations + tool output limits) and structured error codes for troubleshooting.
